speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they first began? Also, have you recently started or changed any psychiatric medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned a movement disorder, but you didn't specify what it looks like. Are you experiencing a constant muscle stiffness, a resting tremor, or involuntary repetitive movements like grimacing or tongue protrusion?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing those symptoms; the inability to remain still and constant restlessness is characteristic of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Do you feel this internal urge to move is constant, or does it fluctuate throughout the day, and have you tried any specific remedies to alleviate it?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of recent risperidone initiation and the classic symptoms of inner restlessness and pacing, I am highly suspicious of drug-induced akathisia. To confirm this clinical diagnosis, I will observe your physical exam for objective signs of motor restlessness. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
